newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end down, but seen firm.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end down, but seen firm.

text.p: South African shares finished the week down on Friday, but hectic trade saw the bourse post a new record in terms of turnover and stocks were seen moving firmly into next week.

The market took a slight knock from Wall Street-inspired falls on most global markets and comments from Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals that monetary policy may need to be tightened to curb credit growth. But dealers said the trend of the market was still upward.
The all-share index ended off 15.9 points at 7,072.0 and industrials lost 19.4 points to 8,406.0.

However, the day saw huge volumes of shares flowing through the market with a new record of 1.506 billion rands worth of stocks being traded. The previous high was 1.447 billion on February 13 earlier this year.
Volumes were boosted by a steady flow of asset swaps, most notably from tobacco concern Richemont Ltd, and the flotation of chicken restaurant Nando's Ltd.
The gold index had a better day as bullion steadied and some buying crept into the market, but dealers said there were no signs of any major change in attitude to the battered counters.
Gold shares ended up 4.5 points to 1,235.0.
